objective: Use the allowed values on each side at fixed local boundary bits to decide whether splitting one crossing Boolean name preserves all boundary triples; give witness assembly, the difference for outer-only decisions and the cost of computing the supports.
status: Proved: Splitting one shared Boolean choice preserves a boundary triple exactly when an empty local support excludes the split triple or the two supports intersect. Complete witnesses can be reconstructed with separate searches over the internally mixed-sign pads.
title: An exact test for dropping equality at a shared boundary choice
